t: You're facing the Buxton Memorial Fountain, a Gothic-style monument that is also a working drinking fountain. It commemorates the emancipation of slaves in the British Empire in 1834, and in particular the part British parliamentarians played in the abolition campaign. Charles Buxton, a brewer, philanthropist, writer and member of Parliament, is named as its designer here. Samuel Sanders Teulon, a Gothic Revival architect known for his polychrome brickwork, is also credited with the design. Together they gave London a memorial to abolition that people can still drink from.
